observations: Two photos show a large, dark solar panel standing upright on dirt ground.
The panel surface shows a grid of photovoltaic cells and thin busbars.
A watermark reading 'INNOSON GLOBAL GROUP' is visible across the center of both photos.
Another panel leans against a wall in the background of both photos.
No manufacturer brand, model number, or wattage label is legible on the panel.
The seller's text lists solar panels, inverters, batteries, and charge controllers, but only panels appear in the images.

claims.evidence: Photos show a panel but cannot verify quality, output, or condition.
photo 0 and photo 1 show a photovoltaic module.

risks.risk: Hidden cell cracks, delamination, or internal damage obscured by surface reflections.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the panel face in direct, angled light, or an electroluminescence/flash test video.

risks.risk: Wattage and electrical output are unknown; the panel may be low capacity or non-functional.
risks.proof: Photo of the rear label showing model and wattage, or a video of voltage/current output under sunlight.
risks.if_unproven: as an untested panel of unknown wattage.

risks.risk: Age and prior usage are unknown; it may be old or second-hand with degraded performance.
risks.proof: Photo of a manufacturing date sticker or original purchase receipt.

proof_requests: Photo of the back label showing brand, model, and wattage.
Video of the panel in sunlight showing voltage and current output.
Close-up of the panel surface to check for cracks or delamination.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a solar panel from the photos, so it can be priced at its worst case as untested and unknown wattage; no missing shot prevents a worst-case price.
